classification.habit: Succulent, branched climbing or scrambling shrub/vine
classification.habitat: Dry tropical and subtropical regions; commonly found on hedges, rocks and disturbed ground
classification.distribution: Widely distributed in India and reported from other South Asian regions.

identification.description: A distinctive succulent climber with quadrangular, jointed green stems; tendrils arise at nodes and small leaves occur on young shoots.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial succulent climber/scrambler with conspicuously four-angled stems and regularly spaced nodes.
identification.root: Fleshy root system; crude-drug authentication should follow the applicable pharmacopoeial or institutional standard.
identification.stem: Characteristic quadrangular, fleshy, jointed green stem; nodes are conspicuous and may bear tendrils and leaves.
identification.leaf: Simple leaves on young shoots, generally ovate to heart-shaped with a somewhat fleshy texture.
identification.flower: Small flowers occur in axillary or opposite clusters; detailed floral authentication should use authenticated material.
identification.fruit: Small globose berry, becoming darker on maturity.
identification.seed: Small seeds contained within the berry; seed-level identification is secondary for the commonly used stem drug.
identification.bark: Stem surface is green and succulent rather than forming a conventional woody bark.
identification_points: Stem is the commonly used medicinal part

therapeutic_actions: Traditional use as a strengthening/supportive drug
therapeutics.dose: Not populated; use an authenticated formulation-specific source.
therapeutics.precautions: Fractures require appropriate medical assessment, reduction/immobilisation when indicated, and follow-up; the herb should not replace orthopaedic care.
therapeutics.contraindications: No universal contraindication statement added without source-level verification.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Published reviews report multiple phytochemical groups; constituent profiles vary by plant material and extraction method.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Cissus quadrangularis is widely studied for bone and musculoskeletal applications. Reviews describe experimental and traditional evidence, but this educational dossier does not convert those findings into a clinical efficacy claim.
modern_information.safety_notes: Evidence and safety depend on preparation and patient context. Fracture management must not be delayed in favour of herbal self-treatment.

student.quick_revision: Asthishrunkhala (Cissus quadrangularis L., Vitaceae) is a succulent climber recognized by its four-angled jointed stem; the stem is the principal traditional medicinal part and is associated with asthisandhanaka use.

teaching_points: Demonstrate the quadrangular stem before discussing therapeutic claims.
Relate the Sanskrit/common names to traditional asthi-sandhana use without presenting them as proof of efficacy.
Compare fresh stem morphology with dried crude drug.
discussion_points: Discuss traditional fracture care versus modern fracture management.
Review the difference between experimental evidence and clinical evidence.
practical_points: Use authenticated fresh material for morphology practicals.
Record stem cross-section, nodes, tendrils and leaf arrangement.
Do not substitute unrelated succulent climbers for the crude drug.

doctor.quick_reference: Cissus quadrangularis L.; Vitaceae; commonly used part is stem. Traditional profile in this project: Madhura rasa, Laghu-Ruksha guna, Ushna virya, Madhura vipaka. For fracture cases, use only as an adjunct to appropriate fracture care.
doctor.dose: Not supplied in this educational dossier.
key_precautions: Do not substitute herbal treatment for fracture reduction, immobilisation or follow-up.
